response.sql: WITH qualifying AS (SELECT DISTINCT ID FROM Laboratory WHERE `U-PRO` = '-' AND RA = '-'), per_patient AS (SELECT l.ID, AVG(l.PT) AS avg_pt, AVG(l.TAT - l.TAT2) AS avg_diff FROM Laboratory l JOIN qualifying q ON q.ID = l.ID GROUP BY l.ID) SELECT AVG(avg_pt) AS avg_of_avg_pt, AVG(avg_diff) AS avg_of_avg_tat_diff FROM per_patient;

assumptions.assumption: TAT - TAT2 is computed per record only where both values are non-null (NULL difference is ignored); the per-patient average is over those records.

Patients whose per-patient average is NULL (no non-null PT, or no record with both TAT and TAT2) are excluded from the corresponding outer average, as the request says to ignore missing values at every step.

alternatives.interpretation: Compute the TAT minus TAT2 average as AVG(TAT) - AVG(TAT2) per patient, so each column is averaged over its own non-null records independently rather than only over records where both are present.
alternatives.sql: WITH qualifying AS (SELECT DISTINCT ID FROM Laboratory WHERE `U-PRO` = '-' AND RA = '-'), per_patient AS (SELECT l.ID, AVG(l.PT) AS avg_pt, AVG(l.TAT) - AVG(l.TAT2) AS avg_diff FROM Laboratory l JOIN qualifying q ON q.ID = l.ID GROUP BY l.ID) SELECT AVG(avg_pt) AS avg_of_avg_pt, AVG(avg_diff) AS avg_of_avg_tat_diff FROM per_patient;
